2. The first respondent which is a nationalised Bank and, as such a financial institution within the meaning of section 2 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 hereinafter referred to as the said Act had obtained a decree for recovery of loan money of Taka 9,40,140.14.00 from the appellant and others with interest at the rate of 18%. Several properties of the judgment-debtors were mortgaged as security for the loan taken by them from the decree holder. The decree being laid in execution in the said court one of the mortaged properties was sold in auction on 28.4.92 and it was purchased by respondent No. 10 at price of Taka 7,02,300.00. The appellant thereupon made an application under Order 21 rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the sale on the ground of fraud and material irregularities in publishing and conducting the sale. The prayer was opposed by the decree-holder as well as the auction purchaser. After a hearing the Artha Rin Adalat, by an order dated 23.9.92, rejected the said application. Being aggrieved the applicant-judgment debtor preferred this appeal. 

 6. One might notice from above that the object in passing this Act is to provide a speedy remedy for recovery of loans advanced by the financial institutions and to save the institutions from protracted litigation under the Code of Civil Procedure in the ordinary courts of law. Sub-section (4) of section 5 provides that notwithstanding anything contained in any other law all cases relating to recovery of loans of the financial institutions must be filed before an Artha Rin Adalat and the same shall be disposed of by the said Court. Sub-section (4) provides that an Artha Rin Adalat will have the powers and jurisdiction of a civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure subject to the provisions of this Act. Sub-section (5) provides that the proceeding before the Artha Rin Adalat shall be governed by the Code of Civil Procedure unless there is anything to the contrary in this Act Sub-section (1) of section 6 provides that the proceeding, order, judgment and decree of an Artha Rin Adalat shall be final subject to the provision for appeals in section 7, while section 7 itself provides appeal only in respect of a judgment, decree and final order upon an application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure and not from any other order of the Adalat. The proviso to the section clearly prohibits appeal from an ad interim order of the Adalat 

 9. Judging the provisions of section 7 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 in the light of the principles enunciated in the aforesaid cases we are of the view that the Code of Civil Procedure is not applicable for the purpose of an appeal against an order of the Artha Rin Adalat, not being a decree, judgment or final order under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In that view of the matter the impugned order being neither a decree, a judgment or a final order under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code but only an ad interim order, is not appealable. The objection is therefore, sustained.
